newsitem.title: USA: Tessco stock plunges after earnings forecast.
newsitem.headline: Tessco stock plunges after earnings forecast.

text.p: Tessco Technologies Inc. stock lost a third of its value Tuesday after the distributor of wireless telephone equipment said earnings for the lastest quarter would not meet analysts' estimates.
Tessco shares tumbled $11 to $21.50 in early trading on Nasdaq, where it was the second-biggest loser of the session.

Tessco, based in Sparks, Md., said after the stock market closed on Monday that it expected earnings for its fiscal fourth quarter to fall between 10 cents and 15 cents a share, well below analysts' average forecast of 24 cents a share.
A year earlier Tessco earned $1.1 million, or 24 cents a share, on sales of $27.3 million.

The company said the earnings shortfall came after it ended sales of products from Andrew Corp., a maker of antennas, transmission lines and other gear, which accounted for 28 percent of sales about $92 million in fiscal 1996.

"Though we successfully converted a substantial portion of the Andrews business to competitive products and reduced Andrew profit contribution by almost two-thirds, we were unable to make a full transition," Chairman Robert Barnhill said in a statement.
Tessco stopped selling nearly all Andrew products after Jan. 1.
Tessco earned $4 million, or 88 cents a share, for the year ended on March 29, 1996.
